title: 2007 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 8
statement:
Determine the largest positive integer \(n\) such that there exist positive integers \(x, y, z\) so that

\[n^{2}=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}+2 x y+2 y z+2 z x+3 x+3 y+3 z-6\]

solutions.text: 8. The given equation rewrites as \(n^{2}=(x+y+z+1)^{2}+(x+y+z+1)-8\). Writing \(r=x+y+z+1\), we have \(n^{2}=r^{2}+r-8\). Clearly, one possibility is \(n=r=8\), which is realized by \(x=y=1, z=6\). On the other hand, for \(r>8\), we have \(r^{2}<r^{2}+r-8<(r+1)^{2}\).
